text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
VJESNIK
- Transitional Adminstrator for Serb-run Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein called the elections in the region for April 13.
- Croatian government has started preparatons for the rebuilding of the Eastern Slavonian capital of Vukovar. Its officials will assess the damage next week.
- Serbs in Eastern Slavonia have put 350 Croats on a list of alleged war criminals.

- Some 275,092 citizens or six percent of the population are jobless, most of them in Zagreb and Split. Their number is on the rise, but if the government used all Croatia's resources, there could be 50,000 unemployed less.
- Revival of tourist trade in the country could cause real chaos as the current hotel and catering staff is not adequately educated or skillful to meet demands of modern tourist demand.
- Average net salary in Zagreb totalled 2,534 kuna in December 1996, or up 3.39 percent from a month before. Highest average net salary of 3,697 kuna was paid by the state water board.
- Cargo handling at Rijeka port shrinks to 2.4 million tonnes in 1996 from 3.6 million a year before.
- Telecoms components maker RIZ-TU d.d. to be liquidated, says director Vlado Radman. The company will later be restructured to produce for Defence Ministry.

- Some 140,000 Croatian and foreign yachts and boats are to sail in Croatia's Adriatic this summer, says Transport Minsiter Zeljko Luzavec at the inauguration of the International Nautical Fair in Rijeka.
VECERNJI LIST

- The government begins to pay back its average 300 kuna debt to each pensioner representing an equivalent of a comparable rise in wages for the past two years that was not translated into pension growth.
- Croatia to impose stricter control of foreign accounts to prevent money laundering through off-shore companies.
- The banking sector may see more mergers and acquisitions in the coming years as competition grows.
- Intercompany debts top eight billion kuna in January.
- Stock Exchange: Trading in public debt refinancing bonds took the spotlight last week with 438 million kuna turnover. Bankers Trust said to have been buying heavily.
- Konzum grocery chain, part of private Agrokor food group, opens three more stores in the centre of Zagreb.
- Banking news: R. Zagorac appointed new board president of Ilirija Banka, replacing N. Vuksan. Karlovacka Banka gets new supervisory board, headed by J. Devlahovic of brewery Karlovacka Pivovara.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA

- Hotelier Solaris from Sibenik at the Adriatic coast is to sue German IFOR contingent for 139,703 German marks damage caused by German soldiers during their year-long stay in Solaris camping site in 1996.
- Trade union of agriculture and food industry workers appeals to the government to lift a ban on sugar imports and allow import of glucose and fructose.
- Croatian Economy Minister Davor Stern and his British counterpart Ian Lang signed an agreement on investment protection and promotion in London.
- Fima brokerage approached shareholders controlling 25 percent of rehabilitated Rijecka Banka with an offer to buy their shares at 64 kuna each. Ultimate buyer unknown.
- AAA-rated Bank Austria to open this spring after reaching a cooperation agreement with Dalmatinska Banka.
- Coastal city of Split may buy a 200 million German marks system for waste control and disposal from German-Croatian company PKA-Ekoloski Inzenjering. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
